recipes.name: Sweet Hot Mustard Chicken Wings
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds chicken wings, separated at joints, tips discarded
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil; coat the aluminum foil with cooking spray.
Arrange the wings on the prepared baking sheet so they do not touch; season with salt.
Bake in the preheated oven until browned and crispy on top, about 20 minutes. Flip the wings with tongs and cook until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 20 minutes more.

Stir together the Dijon mustard, yellow mustard, honey, cider vinegar, salt, pepper, and hot sauce in large mixing bowl. Add the wings to the bowl and toss with a spatula to coat evenly. Allow to sit for about five minutes and toss again to re-coat. Transfer to a plate to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Hot Mustard Chicken Wings
raw_recipe.description: If you are as burned-out on the basic Buffalo-style chicken wing recipe as I am, then this recipe's for you. The hot, sweet, mustardy glaze is a very welcome change of pace from traditional style. Enjoy!

review.reviewBody: Made exactly per recipe. Awesome. Wings were tender and juicy, but most importantly, the flavors were great. A very nice sweet-hot-mustard combination, a great change to the tradtional wing (if there is such a thing).

I have made the sauce this way (5 stars) and then the second time I changed the hot sauce to wing sauce (Sweet Baby Rays) and added 1/2 cup to the rest of the ingredients.(5 stars, as well). Tasted, and added a little more honey. It was devine!! Thanks again for the great recipe

The first time I made this and it was delicious. Tonight I made it again. I didn't have Dijon mustard. So, as usual, I had to improvise, I used extra yellow mustard to replace the Dijon. I also added some garlic power and onion power. My family loved, loved, loved it. Then I also had a chicken breast left over and my son heated it up and stirred it into the sauce. This sauce is a must for chicken from now on.

I actually didn't have any "yellow" mustard in the house. I ended up using a rounded teaspoon of Coleman's, a rounded teaspoon of spicy brown, and the dijon.
I also only used 1/3 of the honey. 
All of the flavors were noticeable. First the mustard then the sweetness topped off with a perfect spiciness. 
This recipe is definitely a keeper although I will try yellow mustard with the Coleman's (I don't want to lose the heat it gives off). Keep it up Chef John, you rock!
I used 3 Tsp spicy mustard, 1/4 cup of honey and 3Tsb of Franks hot sauce on 1lb of wings. The sauce was amazing.

I really like this baked-wing alternative! Two alterations I made were (1) I soaked my wings in clder vinegar for about 5 hours - the time to and from church today - and (2) I used all 1/4 c. of my homemade mustard instead of the 50-50 split Chef John used. YUMMY YUM YUM, wings for the tum!!!

I'm not a big fan of mustard based sauces or dressings, but I LOVED this recipe! We like things spicy and grilled at my house so I increased the hot sauce for extra burn and grilled the wings, basting them as they cooked. It works great on boneless breasts or strips too. A real keeper!

SAUCE ME! I was looking for a sauce for my wings that I had already made tonight. I found the sauce recipe and although I modified it I could still tell that it would have been good as is...(4 stars) but with the substituted items I used...I thought it KICKED it UP! Sriracha mustard, spicy brown mustard and a teaspoon of regular mustard...along with the BRAGGS apple cider vinegar. It was spicy, sweet and ummami! (5 stars with the substitutions)

Yum! I just used this mix to baste chicken drumsticks for lunch and they were so tasty. I can’t wait to try it on chicken wings as the recipe intends, though I think i will stick to basting them as they cook rather than mixing it through afterwards.
Next time I will return it to the oven after each time I coat it with sauce. I think that would be really nice.

Is there a support group to stop eating these? They are great.
I would suggest making a double sauce batch. One for cooking and the other for dipping.
..had no apple vinegar and used balsamic instead.

Not quite the recipe I was after but really good and I make it often. Was a bit lacking in something which is why 4 stars. I found that using the old fashion dijon with the larger seeds worked better, plus a heaping tbsp of Cajun spices (not Creole). Cajon has more flavour than heat so didn't change the heat of the recipe just added the missing "something" it needed.
Love this change from traditional wings and so simple!!

Very flavorful, not too hot. A nice change. I normally make his Panda wings or ginger garlic. These were good, without being hot. Lots of flavor. Add more pepper notes if you like the heat. These went over well with all because of the lack of heat. I recommend this recipe, but add more spice if you are a hot pepperhead
This a great recipe!
Family and friends loved these wings! Nice alternative to Buffalo Wings, or just when you want something different.
Delicious! All I did different was add in more hot sauce
Absolutely supurb!! This recipe seemed to easy to be true - not the case!! I will be making these once a week!??????
Best I've ever had. I didn't have any hot sauce, so added a little cayenne powder to sauce. Just divine!!!!!
Never thought to use mustard as a marinade.
